title: Riverina domestic firewood collection permit
summary: This page provides information on obtaining a permit to collect firewood for domestic use in specific parts of the Riverina region.
intro:
Removing firewood from national parks in NSW is usually not allowed. However, in parts of the Riverina, people can collect firewood for home use if they have a permit and follow strict rules, including:

The Riverina permit is only available to permanent NSW residents who live in the Riverina Bioregion or Balranald Shire. Each household can collect up to 6 tonnes of firewood per year. The permit is valid for 20 days from the date of purchase.

People collecting firewood must follow all permit conditions and park rules while in the park, including staying within open areas and respecting the natural environment. Collection may be paused if there are park closures, fire risk, safety issues or other conservation and operational needs.

Permits can be applied for and purchased online. Refer to the NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service website.
who_can_apply: Must be a permanent NSW resident.
Must live in the Riverina Bioregion or Balranald Shire.
what_you_need: Adherence to all permit conditions and park rules (e.g., staying within open areas and respecting the natural environment).
